title: Product Standards and Margins of Trade: Firm-Level Evidence
research_question: How do restrictive product standards imposed by importing countries affect exporters' behavior across different margins of trade — specifically, the probability of participating in (or exiting) a foreign market, the value of exports conditional on participation, and export prices? Do these effects vary systematically with the size of the exporting firm?
data_description: The analysis combines two main data sources. The first is firm-level export data from French Customs covering all firms located in France over 1995–2005 (estimations focus on 1996–2005 due to lag construction), recording export values by firm, destination country, and product at the 8-digit Combined Nomenclature level, aggregated to HS4 headings. The second is the WTO database on Specific Trade Concerns (STCs) raised in the Sanitary and Phyto-Sanitary (SPS) Committee, which records 312 concerns over 1995–2011, including the imposing country, raising country, HS4 products covered, year raised, and resolution status. Applied tariff data come from TRAINS. The unit of observation is the firm–HS4 product–destination–year. The sample is restricted to extra-EU destinations, excludes services, retains above-median destination markets, and keeps firm-product-destination combinations exporting at least four years.
institutional_context: Sanitary and Phyto-Sanitary (SPS) measures are domestic regulations addressing health, safety, and environmental concerns that may legitimately address market failures but can also act as barriers to trade by raising fixed and/or variable costs of exporting. Within the WTO, the SPS Committee provides a forum where members can raise 'specific trade concerns' regarding measures (in force or draft) imposed by trading partners that they perceive as substantial obstacles to trade. Concerns identify the imposing country, products covered (HS4), year raised, and whether resolved. Roughly 45% of concerns over 1996–2005 were resolved, often through informal agreements rather than formal disputes, with average resolution time of about three years. Concerns span animal health, food safety, plant health, and other issues, and may target measures perceived as discriminatory, non-transparent, or disproportionately burdensome, including for specific firm types.

key_variables.treatment: firms that meet the new product standards
key_variables.control: firms that do not meet the new product standards

_legacy_v1_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The implementation of product standards positively influences firms' export behavior, enhancing both the intensive and extensive margins of trade.
_legacy_v1_ground_truth.main_effect: Increase in export volumes and values for firms meeting the standards
